name: How do I compare bids for exterior remodeling?

mainEntity.name: How should I compare bids for an exterior remodel so I do not miss hidden scope items?
mainEntity.text: How should I compare bids for an exterior remodel so I do not miss hidden scope items?

acceptedAnswer.text: Comparing exterior remodel bids correctly means looking far beyond the bottom-line price. Bids should be matched against the same scope of work, material specifications, permit responsibilities, demolition details, waterproofing steps, cleanup, and inspection coordination. A lower bid often means something important was excluded, such as flashing upgrades, patching hidden damage, disposal, or final finish work. Homeowners should verify whether the bid includes allowances for fixtures and specialty materials, and whether the contractor has assumed any structural or repair conditions. If the project involves windows, stucco, siding, roofing, or hardscape, make sure each contractor is pricing the same systems and not using vague descriptions. It helps to ask for line-item clarity on labor, materials, and exclusions. The best bid is not necessarily the lowest one; it is the one that most clearly matches the actual scope with the fewest surprises. This is especially important in exterior work because hidden conditions often appear after demolition and can significantly change the final cost.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare bids by scope, materials, permit responsibility, demolition, waterproofing, inspections, cleanup, and contingency allowances, not just total price. The cheapest bid often leaves out site protection, flashing, repair work, or finish details. A fair comparison uses the same drawings, same specs, and the same assumptions for every contractor.
